title: Combined Vaginal Hysterectomy and Laparoscopic Sacrocolpopexy with Mesh Placement: Analysis of Complication Rates, Clinical Outcomes, and Patient Satisfaction
summary:
We developed a specialized surgical technique in which the uterus is first removed through the vagina. Afterwards, a supporting synthetic mesh is inserted through the vagina and attached to the remaining supporting structures of the uterus and to the back wall of the vagina. The mesh is then temporarily positioned in the space behind the uterus within the pelvis. The vagina is subsequently closed. In the next step, using minimally invasive surgery through small abdominal incisions, the previously inserted mesh is fixed to the region of the sacrum in order to provide long-term support for the pelvic organs. Finally, the lining of the abdominal cavity is closed using the same minimally invasive approach. If additional repair or tightening of the vaginal walls is required, this is performed individually depending on the patient’s situation.
The aim of this study is to evaluate whether this surgical technique is feasible and safe and whether it can improve pelvic organ prolapse and the associated symptoms.
The study will be conducted exclusively at our center. It is a non-interventional study, meaning that no additional medical intervention will be performed for study purposes. The study consists of two parts: first, the analysis of existing clinical data collected in the past, and second, a follow-up assessment of participants using standardized questionnaires and a clinical examination to evaluate the severity of any possible recurrent pelvic organ prolapse.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients who underwent vaginal hysterectomy with laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy between 2018 and 2025, combined with prospective follow-up and questionnaire assessment (PFIQ-7, PFDI-20)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who underwent both laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy and simultaneous vaginal hysterectomy between 2018 and 2025.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who had previously undergone a hysterectomy.
